subject: Subprocessor responsibilities, incident escalation & cross-border transfer clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@cloudsafe.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Cho <audit@cloudsafe.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Subprocessor responsibilities and incident escalation — SOC/SIG evidence

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. As part of CloudSafe's procurement SIG review we're mapping who owns what for data at rest, key management, logs/telemetry, and model artifacts when Redwood serves requests on behalf of our customers. We also need to confirm the operational escalation path in the event of a suspected subprocessor compromise (who is contacted, expected MTTR, and contract-level responsibilities).

Could you share your current subprocessor registry with the following columns: provider, service type, data categories processed, encryption at rest (Y/N), KMS custody, cross-border transfers (yes/no + countries), and incident point-of-contact? A CSV is ideal.

Also: we have a tight deadline for SOC/SIG evidence next week — can you confirm whether you can provide the SIG-Lite artifact and at least one attestation for KMS ownership?

Appreciate a brief reply and the registry by Wednesday 6/10 if possible.

Thanks,
Elena
Information Security Manager
CloudSafe, Inc.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@cloudsafe.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 17:43:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor responsibilities and incident escalation — SOC/SIG evidence

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the clear column requirements. Attaching our current subprocessor registry (CSV) plus the SIG-Lite evidence bundle you requested. See the top-level notes in the CSV for a short summary of responsibilities.

Quick highlights:
- KMS custody: Redwood uses customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and our hosted customers may opt into customer-managed keys via our KMS integration; by default Redwood uses AWS KMS for envelope keys for hosted workloads.
- Model artifacts: storing model binaries and checkpoints is handled by our model-store provider (ModelVault Inc.); Redwood does not share raw customer data with ModelVault — only encrypted artifacts and hashes.
- Telemetry/logs: aggregated telemetry is retained in our telemetry backend (LogixOps) with PII redaction rules; raw request logs are considered customer data and retained per contract.
- Cross-border transfers: most subprocessors operate in multiple regions; CSV flags explicit country-level transfers for EU/UK/APAC.
- Incident escalation: primary contact for subprocessor incidents is our Security Ops oncall (secops@redwood.com). For escalations that impact customer data, we engage account security and the customer's security contact within 2 hours of confirmation and provide ETA updates every 4 hours until mitigation; target MTTR depends on severity but initial containment target is 6–12 hours for critical incidents.

Attachments:
- redwood_subprocessors_registry_20260608.csv (table with provider/service/data categories/KMS/countries/PoC)
- sig-lite-evidence-20260608.pdf (SIG-Lite checklist + attestation snippets)

If you want, Markus can give a short call to walk through the KMS custody nuances for Private vs Hosted.

Best,
Priya
Sr. Security Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Cho <audit@cloudsafe.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor responsibilities and incident escalation — SOC/SIG evidence

Priya,

Thanks for the quick turnaround — the CSV and SIG-Lite look useful. Two quick follow-ups from our audit team: 
1) Can you explicitly confirm who holds encryption keys for hosted customer data in the US region (is it Redwood-managed AWS KMS keys or do customers always have the option to bring their own keys)?
2) For the ModelVault subprocessor, please confirm whether model artifact backups are replicated to any third country outside the EU/US boundary (we need to know if APAC replication occurs and where).

Also — we're asking that the incident escalation POA includes a phone number for primary incident contact (not just a mailbox). Can you add that to the CSV?

If you can reply by EOD Wednesday we'll mark this as green for now.

Aaron
CloudSafe Audit Team

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Cho <audit@cloudsafe.com>, Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@cloudsafe.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor responsibilities and incident escalation — SOC/SIG evidence

Hi Aaron / Elena — Markus here, I own vendor security at Redwood. Quick answers inline: 

1) Hosted customer data encryption (US region): by default Redwood-generated envelope keys are managed in our AWS account (AWS KMS) for hosted API customers. We offer BYOK/CMK for enterprise customers via our KMS integration; that option is selectable at onboarding and is documented in the Dedicated/Private onboarding guide (link below).

2) ModelVault replication: ModelVault maintains primary storage in US-East and replicates backups to EU-West for redundancy. There is no APAC replication for the ModelVault artifact backups associated with Redwood model-store as of the current configuration. We'll include an explicit 'replication_countries' column in the CSV.

3) Incident contact phone: adding primary SecOps oncall phone: +1-415-555-0192 (US daytime) and secondary: +1-650-555-0123. We will append these to the registry and re-upload.

Next steps: Priya will push an updated CSV to the same Drive folder with the replication countries and phone numbers; we'll also drop a short note in RINF-4532 describing the KMS options and where BYOK is enforceable. If you'd like a 20-min call to close questions, I'm available Thu 6/11 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Vendor Security
Redwood Inference
